Learning takes repetition. Through a process called neuroplasticity, your brain adapts by strengthening existing connections between neurons and forming new ones.

Each time you revisit a skill or piece of information, you reinforce these neural pathways, making it easier for your brain to recall and use what you’ve learned. This is why repetition plays such an important role in retaining information and building new skills.

outliers.title: Capsule Endoscopy: A Pill-Sized Camera's Journey Through Your Entire Gut
outliers.description:
What happens when you swallow a camera? In just 10 seconds, follow a capsule endoscope through the esophagus, stomach, duodenum, small intestine and colon, and see what it sees along the way.
Capsule endoscopy lets doctors examine the small intestine, an area that's hard to reach with standard scopes, without sedation or an invasive procedure. The capsule is about the size of a large vitamin pill, takes thousands of images as it travels, and is passed naturally in stool.
In reality the journey takes 8 to 12 hours. This clip is a time-lapse visualization.
⚠️ AI-generated educational animation.
